To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed an efficient statistical static timing analysis (STAC) algorithm for the statistical analysis of timing paths that accounts for correlations in process parameters and path delays and can be used for the statistical analysis and optimization of circuits in the presence of process variations.
we have developed an efficient block-based algorithm to compute statistical timing information for correlated process parameters.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a statistical timing analysis methodology for sub-100 nm technologies that can accurately model both process variations and interconnect coupling.
the development of efficient statistical timing analysis techniques that can accurately predict timing distributions in nanometer technologies.

the following questions: (1) how to model the statistical timing analysis problem in an efficient manner that can account for the correlation of process parameters; (2) how to model dominant interconnect coupling effect; (3) how to model re-converging timing paths.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed STAC algorithm is a very effective method for statistical timing analysis.
the proposed algorithm provides a practical, efficient and accurate statistical static timing analysis solution for sub-100 nm designs.
STAC is the first statistical static timing analysis tool that can efficiently handle both inter-die process variations and intra-die correlations for a wide variety of process technologies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the proposed algorithm is capable of handling both inter-die variations and intra-die variations with correlation, while maintaining the efficiency for the computation of mean, variance and covariances of the timing information.
we present a new block-based statistical static analysis algorithm that can efficiently handle both intra-die and inter-die parameter variations with correlation.
the proposed method can provide a tight upper bound for the worst-case circuit delay while the computation cost is comparable to a conventional STA algorithm.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the correlation information is crucial for statistical timing analysis.
a block-based approach is not only sufficient but also more efficient than path-based approaches for the statistical timing analysis of modern circuits.

the statistical timing analysis problem can be solved in an efficient way that can account for both intra-die and inter-die correlations, and the proposed algorithm can be used as an effective tool for statistical timing analysis in future technologies.
